Sottile e fragile, di una solidità sconvolgente. Piccola come microscopiche deflagrazioni di bolle e d’aromi a bordo palato, capricciosa e seducente come una lolita d’altri tempi e d’altri luoghi, piccante e innocente. Con eleganza si accosta alle labbra con un ingresso secco e finemente effervescente: come una donna di gran classe, già indossa pochi accessori (ma di carattere) che lasciano nella memoria un segno rosaceo indelebile. In punta di piedi sparge attorno dei tratti di rosa, di piccolo frutto cui si accompagnano un chiacchiericcio sussurrato che cattura; e un lato oscuro affascinante in cui la tenebra non prevarica mai la freschezza pungente di giardino orientale. Sarà per le virtù alchemiche di un grano antico e miracoloso, o per quel profumo segreto che viene da lontano e porta sempre con sé: ma ci ha preso il cuore, e lo sa stringere, ungere di balsamo e straziare ogni volta che in silenzio arriva, e dopo poco se ne va.

Schwarzbier has been around since at least the 16th century and was once more widespread than it is today. During the Industrial Revolution in the 19th century it was almost replaced by mass-produced lighter beers. Only a few breweries have preserved the beer style, and it has been experiencing a renaissance for around 30 years.

We use a very special smoked malt for our Aecht Schlenkerla Erle black beer. This is not dried over a beech wood fire as usual, but over an alder wood fire. The alder smoked malt brings a fine, complex smoky flavor to the beer, which is less strong and spicy than our classic smoked beer. A high proportion of roasted malt ensures a pronounced roasted aroma and the dark, almost black color. At 4.3%, Aecht Schlenkerla Erle has slightly less alcohol, but has a strong taste.

Our friends at Pomologik are cultivating a new Swedish cider culture. Always whole apples and natural ingredients, spontaneously fermented, using traditional methods that respect the long history of cider making.
 We’ve crafted some delicious beverages that were a true blend of their style and ours (see: Winter Wine and Pearliner), but for our third we went all in on honoring one of the oldest cider making regions in the world. Basque Country is a richly cultured region that lies between Spain and France in the Western Pyrenees mountains where local cider houses known as sagardotegi have been making traditional cider known as sagardo for centuries. Juice from local apple varieties high in acidity and tannins, wild fermented using native yeasts, aged for months in large chestnut barrels with no intervention; Basque cider is as natural as it gets. Rotbier (i.e. red lager) used to be common in Franconia. The city of Nuremberg in particular was known for its Rotbier. Since its production was extremely laborious, Rotbier was replaced in the 19th century by Braunbier (i.e. brown lager) which was produced using modern, simpler brewing methods. It was not until 1997 that the beer style was revived.
 For Aecht Schlenkerla Weichsel Rotbier, the malt is dried over fire with cherry wood (not over beech wood fire as with classic smoked beer). In contrast to the spicy beech-smoked malt, the cherry wood smoked malt has a fruity, almost sweet smoke aroma and provides a copper-red color in the glass. The aroma hops add berry notes to the multi-layered smoke flavor.

We started our beloved Church brewery 5 years ago and the first beer we brewed was a stout. Since then we have built out the church stout program, barrel for barrel. Carefully and obsessively honing our base recipes, hunting down barrels from our favorite spirit makers and developing our post barrel treatment under the working name, CAKEIFICATION. A couple of months ago we felt that we had reached full CAKEIFICATION in a trial and so the search for the perfect barrel was on.

That barrel turned out to be a big (duh) double mashed, long-boil imperial stout aged for a year in fresh Sazerac barrels and then transferred into dripping wet apple brandy barrels for another year. A symphony of expressive barrel, chocolate and caramelized Tarte Tatin.

Over the next coming months this beer underwent a gentle, cold and slow CAKEIFICATION using a spectrum of coconut at different toasting levels, more vanilla than we’ve ever used (Indonesian Java and Madagascan bourbon) and heaps and heaps of toasted peanuts.

The result?

beer.beer_description: Following century old recipes all malts made at the Schlenkerla brewery are dried by wood fire. While for the classic “Aecht Schlenkerla Rauchbier” traditionally beech has been – and still is – used, the malt for “Schlenkerla Oak Smoke” is kilned with oak wood. The resulting Oak Smoke Malt has a smoother and more multi layered smoky note than the intensely aromatic Beech Smoke Malt. The hence complex smokiness in “Schlenkerla Oak Smoke” is paired with the multifaceted bitterness of finest Hallertau aroma hops. With 8% alcohol and amber color it matures for months in the deep brewery cellars underneath Bamberg into a special treat for smoke beer lovers for Christmas.

Michael's Great-Grandmother immigrated to America from Ireland in the 1880s. We took inspiration for this Irish stout from the ingredients used in recipes from around that time: Pale Ale, Amber, and Black malts. These are more flavorful (and expensive) than the unmalted barley that comprises a large portion of most Irish stout recipes today. However, we kept the modern balance of restrained alcohol, invitingly dry-roasty finish, and creamy mouthfeel!

Double Barrel Aged Imperial Stout Blend.

Has it really been eight years? As of writing this we have filled 472 barrels with (mostly) stouts since those early days, and when our birthday comes around we like to dig deep and show off the best of them. This year, after several extended blending sessions, we arrived at this double-barrel aged blend which we believe stands tall without the need for any adjuncts or additions.

This blend pulls from four stouts aged 21–28 months in Thomas H. Handy 15yr Rye, Stagg Jr 8yr, and two Weller 12yr barrels, then transferred into Rare Breed 14yr, French Cognac 6yr, Blanton’s 6yr, and Weller 7yr barrels for an additional 14–24 months.

With 8 total barrels — including wheated bourbons, rye, cognac, and a wide range of age statements — this beer layers spirit character, oak, and malt depth into something rich, intense, and harmonious. Built from three stout brews, it’s greater than the sum of its parts and everything we strive for in a decadent, spirit-forward beer.

Cheers to 8 years — and many more.

We're once again testing out some cool new hops from Yakima Chief, this time in a DDH Modern West Coast IPA! La Dolce Vita showcases Yakima's new hop Dolcita in both T90 & Cryo formats, that showcases flavors reminiscent of peach ring candies and pinapple. We have paired up Dolcita with a Yakima classic Simcoe, in Crop Selected T90 & Dynaboost formats, for more pinapple and grapefruit flavors, alongside HBC 522 carrying flavors of citrus, pine and floral notes. An IPA that bridges the gap between modern and classic West Coast flavors!

For this classic style, we decided to use the "king of German hops" known as Hallertau Mittelfrüh, hence the name. Mittelfrüh translates into "middle-early," which is the optimum time during the harvest season to pluck these hops from their bines. This "noble" hop exhibits gentle floral and herbal flavors with the addition of spice undertones. Mittelfrüh is similar to what you would drink in liters at the numerous beer halls throughout Munich, so drink up and prost!

Rotbier (i.e. red lager) used to be common in Franconia. The city of Nuremberg in particular was known for its Rotbier. Since its production was extremely laborious, Rotbier was replaced in the 19th century by Braunbier (i.e. brown lager) which was produced using modern, simpler brewing methods. It was not until 1997 that the beer style was revived.
 For Aecht Schlenkerla Weichsel Rotbier, the malt is dried over fire with cherry wood (not over beech wood fire as with classic smoked beer). FESTIVAL EDITION ! I love stout. In fact, the first beer I brewed as a homebrewer was a stout.

We started our beloved Church brewery 5 years ago and the first beer we brewed was a stout. Since then we have built out the church stout program, barrel for barrel. Carefully and obsessively honing our base recipes, hunting down barrels from our favorite spirit makers and developing our post barrel treatment under the working name, CAKEIFICATION. A couple of months ago we felt that we had reached full CAKEIFICATION in a trial and so the search for the perfect barrel was on.

That barrel turned out to be a big (duh) double mashed, long-boil imperial stout aged for a year in fresh Sazerac barrels and then transferred into dripping wet apple brandy barrels for another year. A symphony of expressive barrel, chocolate and caramelized Tarte Tatin.

Over the next coming months this beer underwent a gentle, cold and slow CAKEIFICATION using a spectrum of coconut at different toasting levels, more vanilla than we’ve ever used (Indonesian Java and Madagascan bourbon) and heaps and heaps of toasted peanuts.

The result?

Moiré is a blended barrel aged Imperial Stout and Imperial Wheat Stout, aged for 18 to 24 months in Weller bourbon barrels and ex maple Danish rye whiskey barrels. After blending, the beer was given an extended maturation on a generous amount of Blue Vanilla, adding softness, depth and a layered aromatic richness.

The name Moiré refers to the effect that appears when two colours or patterns meet and create something new in between. Here, that idea comes mainly from the way the Blue Vanilla moves through the beer: the dark barrel aged stout forms one layer, while the vanilla brings a brighter, aromatic layer of its own. Together they create a new expression, softer, deeper and more rounded than either element on its own.

Following century old recipes all malts made at the Schlenkerla brewery are dried by wood fire. While for the classic “Aecht Schlenkerla Rauchbier” traditionally beech has been – and still is – used, the malt for “Schlenkerla Oak Smoke” is kilned with oak wood. The resulting Oak Smoke Malt has a smoother and more multi layered smoky note than the intensely aromatic Beech Smoke Malt. The hence complex smokiness in “Schlenkerla Oak Smoke” is paired with the multifaceted bitterness of finest Hallertau aroma hops. With 8% alcohol and amber color it matures for months in the deep brewery cellars underneath Bamberg into a special treat for smoke beer lovers for Christmas.

Together with 3 Sons we schemed this up…

Blended? We blended two beers aged in two different barrels together with a new batch of thick and sweet imperial stout… for this project the perfect match of deep caramel dried fruit barrel aged character, and fresh chocolate roasty notes and sweetness!

Bake Shop? Yes, it’s loaded with tonka beans, two origins of cinnamon, cardamom and home cooked caramelized sugar… on top of that, aged on a no shy amount of three origins of vanilla beans from Uganda, Madagascar and Papua New Guinea. The levels are perfectly balanced - nothing is too much, nothing is too little.

Expect this to be a real sipper with layers and layers of flavours and spices, sweet and sticky that surprises you throughout with balanced barrel character as well as roastiness from the fresh imperial stout.

Just a 100% pleasure to work with 3 Sons on this project!

It’s always a given that when it comes to Birthday Beer time, we’re always going to dip over to the dark side. Who better then to extend an invitation to share knowledge and expertise with than one of the best in the game today when it comes to imperial stouts, and one which we’ve worked closely with since their launch, Azvex? As longtime admirers of their big, decadent pastry stouts, we couldn’t think of anyone better to work with than our friends from just over the water in Liverpool. Working our recipe around the fika breaks we have at Polly’s every working day, we loved the idea of creating the flavour profile of a danish pastry in this beer - utilising the fresh vanilla we’ve applied to our Oat Cream beers, alongside raisin for a subtle fruit sweetness, and a final flourish of cinnamon to balance everything out. Featuring artwork produced by the wonderful local artist and good friend of the brewery Jake Cross, this beer took up a grand total of five separate brew slots in our brewing week, with a ridiculous twenty-four hour slow rolling boil to concentrate all those sugars. the result is a slick, oily and decadent imperial stout - rich in flavour but not cloying, and widely regarded within the brewery as our best imperial stout brewed over our eight year history.
